who: Business and economic historian at the University of Delaware, later Sydney; PhD Harvard 1961.

evidence.says: The authority for Stephen Salsbury identifies the business historian and records his appointment as associate professor of history at Delaware; it lists The State, the Investor, and the Railroad.
The college account of Stephen Salsbury states that he earned his Harvard doctorate in 1961 and later became professor of economic history at Sydney.
The University of Delaware newspaper of February 22, 1971 identifies Stephen Salsbury as professor of history.

notes: The authority affiliation and independently matching Harvard doctorate identify the same historian.

who: Florida historian who taught at Florida State before becoming history professor and chair at UCF; PhD Florida State.

evidence.says: The Jerrell H. Shofner authority identifies the University of Central Florida history professor and author of Nor Is It Over Yet.
The Orlando Sentinel obituary reports a history PhD from Florida State, subsequent teaching at Florida State, and appointment as UCF history professor and chair in 1972.
The Florida Historical Society identifies Jerrell H. Shofner as a Florida historian with a Florida State PhD and a UCF career beginning in 1972.

notes: The Florida State training and teaching connect the AHA supervisor to the UCF historian in the authority record. The later dissertation dates do not establish his continued employment at Florida State.

who: Historian of modern European history, art and culture at UCLA; PhD Princeton 1983.

evidence.says: The Debora Silverman authority explicitly identifies the UCLA professor of modern European history, art and culture, and lists the name Debora Leah Silverman.
UCLA identifies Silverman as its professor of modern European history, art and culture and gives her PhD as Princeton University, 1983.
UCLA lists Marissa Helene Petrou and the Dresden museum dissertation under advisers Theodore Porter and Debora Silverman.

notes: The authority directly names the UCLA historian; her doctorate and supervision of the listed student both match.

who: Historian of ancient Greece, Rome and military history at Cornell; PhD Yale 1979.

evidence.says: The Barry S. Strauss authority identifies the Cornell professor of history and classics and author of The Death of Caesar; Barry Strauss is a recorded name usage.
Cornell identifies Barry Stuart Strauss as a professor in its history department specializing in ancient Greek, Roman and military history.
The publisher biography gives his Yale PhD as 1979 and identifies him as Cornell professor of history and classics.

notes: The authority explicitly identifies the Cornell historian, and the Yale doctorate matches the AHA record.

who: Historian of South Africa at Yale and Miami University, Ohio; PhD Harvard, with conflicting year information.

evidence.says: The authority expands M. W. Swanson to Maynard Swanson and identifies him as associate professor of history at Miami University of Ohio, editor of The Views of Mahlathi (1982).
Miami's faculty memorial identifies Maynard W. Swanson, says he joined Yale history in 1963 and Miami in 1970, and names his edited work The Views of Mahlathi. It gives his Harvard PhD year as 1960.
The University of Cape Town finding aid identifies Maynard William Swanson as professor of African history at Miami University, Oxford, Ohio, researching A. W. G. Champion.

notes: Both AHA institutions and the authority's edited work match. The Miami memorial gives Harvard 1960, whereas own_phd gives 1965; the year discrepancy remains unresolved.

who: Historian of Renaissance and early modern Europe at West Virginia University; PhD UCLA 1997.

evidence.says: The Matthew A. Vester authority records Matthew Allen Vester, a West Virginia University historian who began teaching there in 2000, with graduate training at Virginia and UCLA.
WVU gives Vester's UCLA PhD as 1997 and lists Cole Volman, Catherine Ferrari (2022), and Megan McGee (2018, co-directed) among his PhD students.

notes: The authority affiliation, exact doctorate, and all three listed students identify the same supervisor; dissertation titles vary between the supplied record and faculty page.

who: Historian of African American history, women and the South at Cornell University.

evidence.says: The Margaret Washington authority explicitly identifies the Cornell history professor and author of Sojourner Truth's America, with research in African American history, gender and the South.
The 2018 Oxford Handbook contributor biography identifies Margaret Washington as professor of history and American studies at Cornell and author of Sojourner Truth's America.
Cornell's February 2012 announcement lists history professor Margaret Washington alongside Cornell PhD candidate Candace Katungi in a history symposium.

notes: The authority explicitly names the Cornell historian and her work; institutional and publisher sources place her there during the students' period.

who: Historian of the US West and environmental history at Oregon; PhD history, Wisconsin-Madison 2000.

evidence.says: The Marsha L. (Marsha Lee) Weisiger authority records a history PhD from Wisconsin-Madison in 2000 and the dissertation Dine Bikeyah.
Oregon identifies Marsha Weisiger as professor of history and environmental studies and Dixon Chair of US Western History.
Oregon identifies Marsha Weisiger as one of Hayley Brazier's history research advisers on seafloor infrastructure.

notes: The authority's exact doctorate matches own_phd; Oregon affiliation and the listed student independently connect the supervisor to that historian.
